task: perf_counters.py bootstrap -- kpc/kperf hardware-counter telemetry for PPU-rework stage gates
claim: ctypes binding against kperf.framework + kperfdata.framework is WORKABLE on this macOS version (26.6 / T6041 M4 Max). All required symbols resolve, the full non-privileged setup path (event-database lookup, config-word generation) runs to completion and produces sane output, and the root-gated calls fail with the exact, expected EPERM -- not a load error, not a missing-symbol error, not a crash.

kperf_framework_dlopen.note: file is a dyld-shared-cache stub on disk (nm/file/otool fail on it directly) but ctypes.CDLL() resolves it fine via dyld -- this is normal on macOS 11+.

kperfdata_framework_dlopen.note: kperfdata.framework's kpep_db_create(NULL, ...) loads the CURRENT machine's PMU event database dynamically at runtime. perf_counters.py resolves all 5 target events BY NAME against this live database instead of hardcoding chip-generation-specific config-register encodings, so it is not tied to M4/T6041 specifically.

counter_budget.note: fixed class is always [cycles, instructions] on every Apple Silicon generation to date; our 5 target configurable events exactly fill the 5 configurable slots this chip reports.

configurable_event_resolution.note: kpep_config_add_event + kpep_config_kpc + kpep_config_kpc_map all returned rc=0 for all 5 events; config words above are the ACTUAL output of tonight's run (docs cross-checked against scripts/perf_counters.py --diagnose --json), not hand-derived.

kpc_force_all_ctrs_set(1).note: probed manually during development; NOT called by perf_counters.py -- the task's specified init sequence (kpc_set_counting/kpc_set_config/kpc_set_thread_counting/kpc_get_thread_counters) doesn't need it for the kernel-mediated read path used here.

permission_probe.conclusion: every root-gated call fails EXACTLY at the privilege boundary, with EPERM, after all non-privileged setup (dlopen, symbol bind, event DB lookup, config-word generation, buffer sizing) succeeded. This is the graceful-degradation path perf_counters.py detects via os.geteuid()==0 and reports with the exact sudo command to use.

emu_workload.tape_provenance: full-game-clear action recording banked by the live show (see project memory: GAME COMPLETE 2026-07-27); replayed here purely as a fixed, realistic, deterministic CPU/PPU/APU workload -- recorded originally at frame_skip=4 for gameplay, replayed here 1:1 at frame_skip=1 so '2000 frames' is literal. Trajectory fidelity vs. the original playthrough is NOT required or claimed for this purpose.
emu_workload.note: '1 core only' is structural, not an affinity syscall: a single NESEnvironment stepped serially holds the GIL and spawns no worker threads/Pool. macOS/Apple Silicon has no user-facing hard core-pin API (mach thread affinity tags are a soft hint, largely ignored on Apple Silicon) -- documented as a known limitation, not attempted.

xctrace_fallback_probe.note_on_xcode_select: xcode-select -p points at /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools (no 'xctrace' there); the full Xcode.app is installed separately and xctrace was invoked via its absolute path without changing xcode-select globally.
xctrace_fallback_probe.list_templates: confirmed 'CPU Counters' present among 26 standard templates

record_probe.result: exit 0, produced a full probe.trace bundle
record_probe.developer_mode_note: DevToolsSecurity -status reports 'Developer mode is currently disabled' on this machine, but xctrace record+export both worked anyway for this template/launch mode -- developer mode was NOT required here, contrary to initial assumption.

export_probe.result: exit 0, returned real per-interval uint64 counter arrays (e.g. '0xa09 0x781 0xe70 0x6ca' -> 2569 1921 3696 1738)
export_probe.caveat: columns are raw values from the default 'Guided / CPU Bottlenecks' configuration, not individually labeled to our 5 named events; per-event labeling needs a 'Custom' counter configuration or decoding form.template's metric formulas -- NOT wired tonight, documented as future work only.

xctrace_fallback_probe.conclusion: xctrace is a genuine, verified, no-root-needed fallback path, fully independent of the ctypes/kpc path above. Both paths work; ctypes/kpc is the primary because it produces individually-named counters directly.

not_verified_tonight_deferred_to_root_ru: Actual nonzero counter VALUES (cycles/instructions/L1D/L2TLB/branch) for the emu workload -- every kpc_set_* call is root-gated and returned EPERM as designed; no counter was ever armed long enough to read a real number.

Whether kpc_set_config succeeds as plain root with SIP left ENABLED, or whether it needs SIP disabled. Historical Intel-era docs required disabling SIP for kpc_force_all_ctrs_set specifically; that call is NOT used by this module. Expectation (based on the fact that many shipped Apple Silicon tools -- asitop, powermetrics-adjacent utilities -- program kpc as root with SIP enabled) is that plain sudo suffices, but this is NOT independently confirmed against this exact macOS build.

Fixed-counter slot ordering assumption (index 0 = cycles, index 1 = instructions) -- an architectural convention used across all public Apple Silicon kpc tooling, not independently re-derived from this chip's event database (FIXED events carry no configurable slot mapping to check against). Cross-check first with a trivial spin-loop tomorrow: counter[0] should scale with wall-clock * clock-speed, counter[1] with a known static instruction count.

Whether the 5 chosen configurable events actually produce sane relative magnitudes on a real workload (e.g. branch_mispredictions should be a small fraction of instructions, not the majority) -- basic sanity-check math, not yet run against real numbers.

cli_surface.--bench emu: runs the single-NESEnvironment 2000-frame replay workload (default), with counters when root
cli_surface.--rom / --tape: override the ROM and action-tape paths
cli_surface.--json / --out PATH: machine-readable output, optionally written to a file
cli_surface.--diagnose: binding/event-DB/permission probe only, no workload, safe to run repeatedly without root
cli_surface.--xctrace-recipe: prints the verified Instruments fallback recipe and exits

rust_changes: none -- this task only added a Python module/CLI script; nes_core was used exclusively through the already-installed production wheel's nes_core.NESEnvironment. No cargo check/test run because no Rust source changed.
